proposed.effect: An order of attachment may issue if it could issue out of the Supreme Court in a like case (grounds: NY:CPLR-6201-attachment-grounds), executed only within New York City (NY:CCA-801-provisional-city-only). No injunction, restraining order or restraining notice issues except for chattel recovery, prevention of waste, a CCA 1508 enforcement proceeding, or housing-standards enforcement; no receiver except in an enforcement proceeding, a mortgage foreclosure or an MDL 309(5) action.
proposed.quote: (a) Attachment, arrest, seizure of chattel. An order of attachment or of arrest, a warrant to seize a chattel as provided in § 207 of the lien law, and an order of seizure of a chattel may issue out of this court if such remedy might issue out of supreme court in a like case. (b) Injunction or restraining order. No injunction or restraining order or notice shall issue out of or by this court unless: (1) pursuant to §§ 7102(d), 7103(c) and 7109 of the CPLR, in conjunction with the recovery of a chattel; or (2) pursuant to § 211 of the Real Property Actions and Proceedings law, in conjunction with the prevention of waste; or (3) pursuant to § 1508 of this act, in conjunction with an enforcement proceeding; or (4) pursuant to section three hundred six of the multiple dwelling law, or article fifty-three of the housing maintenance code of the administrative code of the city of New York in conjunction with enforcement of housing standards. (c) Receivers. No receiver shall be appointed by this court except pursuant to § 1508 of this act, relative to an enforcement proceeding, or in an action for the foreclosure of a mortgage on real property, brought pursuant to the provisions of § 203 (b) of this act, or in an action brought pursuant to subdivision five of section three hundred nine of the multiple dwelling law, relative to the appointment of a receiver for the recovery of costs, expenses and disbursements incurred by the city of New York in the elimination or correction of a nuisance or in the removal or demolition of a building pursuant thereto.

reason: Several claims each within the $50,000 limit may be joined and judgment may exceed $50,000; changes whether a large combined balance (rent, damage, guaranty) can stay in Civil Court.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: The landlord's complaint joins several causes of action against a former tenant (for example rent after vacating and physical damage) whose total exceeds $50,000.
proposed.effect: If each cause of action would be within the $50,000 limit if sued separately, the Civil Court has jurisdiction and may render judgment above $50,000 when the excess results solely from the joinder; judgment on a counterclaim is unlimited.
proposed.quote: Where several causes of action are asserted in the complaint and each of them would be within the jurisdiction of the court if sued upon separately, the court shall have jurisdiction of the action. In such case judgment may be rendered by the court in excess of $50,000 if such excess result solely because of such joinder. Nothing herein shall be construed to prevent the court from granting judgment in an unlimited amount on a counterclaim.

reason: Venue of real property actions (title, liens, possession other than summary proceedings); a suit for a lease balance or a deposit is a transitory money action, not a real property action.
Venue of a summary proceeding to recover possession, which is part of how possession is regained before the settlement chain starts; it changes nothing in the account.
Venue for actions by or against the City of New York or the Transit Authority; neither is a party to a market-rate tenancy settlement.
Suing in the wrong county is not fatal; the tenant must move to transfer at or before joinder of issue or waives venue. Changes the consequence of a venue error in the landlord's suit.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: The landlord's balance action (or the tenant's deposit action) is filed in an NYC Civil Court county that is not a proper venue.
proposed.effect: The wrong county is not a jurisdictional defect. The court may transfer on its own motion and must transfer on the defendant's written motion on notice, filed before or at joinder of issue, naming the proper county and stating the facts under oath. Without a timely motion the defendant waives venue.
proposed.quote: The bringing of an action or proceeding in the wrong county shall not be deemed a jurisdictional defect, but the court may of its own motion and must on the motion of a party defendant transfer the action or proceeding to a proper county. The motion by the defendant for such relief must be made in writing and on notice and must be filed with the clerk before or at joinder of issue. It must specify the county to which the defendant desires the action or proceeding to be transferred and must state under oath facts showing that ground exists for such transfer. In the absence of timely motion by the defendant, he shall be deemed to have waived any objection relating to proper venue, except in the case of a real property action.

reason: An NYC Civil Court action is commenced by filing the summons and complaint with the fee (the limitations interposition date) and jurisdiction is acquired by service; the index number must be on the papers served.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: A balance action against a former tenant, or a tenant's deposit action, is brought in the NYC Civil Court regular part.
proposed.effect: It is commenced by filing (delivering to the clerk in the county of suit) the summons and complaint with the CCA 1911 fee; that filing date is the commencement for CPLR 203 (NY:CPLR-203-accrual-interposition). The clerk date-stamps and returns a copy. Jurisdiction over the defendant is acquired only by serving it with the summons and complaint. The actual index number must appear on the summons as served; an omission is cured by stipulation or by leave of court, which is not unreasonably withheld.
proposed.quote: 1. An action is commenced in this court by filing a summons and complaint. A special proceeding is commenced by filing a notice of petition and petition or order to show cause and petition. For purposes of this section, and for purposes of section two hundred three of the civil practice law and rules, filing shall mean the delivery of the summons and complaint, the notice of petition and petition or order to show cause and petition to the clerk of the court in the county in which the action or special proceeding is brought together with any fee required by section nineteen hundred eleven of this act. At the time of filing, the original and a copy of the papers shall be date stamped by the court clerk who shall file the original and maintain a record of the filing and shall return the copy to the party who brought the filing. The clerk shall accept the fee and file the papers as soon as reasonably practicable. 2. Jurisdiction is acquired over a party to an action or special proceeding by service upon such party of a copy of the summons and complaint, the notice of petition and petition or the order to show cause and petition. 3. The actual index number shall be on the summons, notice of petition or order to show cause as served. Failure to include the index number on the papers as served shall be cured by stipulation between the parties or by leave of court, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

reason: Who issues the Civil Court summons and what it must contain (answer with the clerk, the plaintiff's residence address, the attorney's office address); the consumer-credit bilingual summons does not reach a lease balance.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: The landlord sues a former tenant in the NYC Civil Court.
proposed.effect: The summons is issued by the landlord's attorney or, if the landlord appears without an attorney (an individual owner), by the clerk. It directs the tenant to file an answer with the clerk, is in the form the rules prescribe, and states the plaintiff's residence address and, if an attorney issues it, the attorney's office address. The Spanish-and-English summons required in consumer credit transaction actions does not apply to a lease balance (NY:ADJ-lease-balance-not-consumer-credit).
proposed.quote: (a) The summons may be issued by the plaintiff's attorney or, if the plaintiff appears without attorney, by the clerk. (b) The summons shall direct the defendant to file his answer with the clerk and shall otherwise be in such form as may be provided by rule. It shall contain the residence address of the plaintiff and, if it is issued by the plaintiff's attorney, the latter's office address. (c) Notwithstanding the provisions of section 731 of the real property actions and proceedings law, regarding issuance by an attorney, the notice of petition in a summary proceeding to recover possession of real property shall be issued only by a judge or the clerk of the court. The original petition shall be filed with the clerk at the time the notice of petition is issued. (d) The summons served in an action arising from a consumer credit transaction must be printed legibly in both Spanish and English.

reason: Fixes the tenant's time to answer a Civil Court summons (20 days after personal delivery in the city; otherwise 30 days after proof of service is filed), which sets when a default judgment becomes available.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: The landlord serves a Civil Court summons on a former tenant (or the tenant serves one on the landlord).
proposed.effect: Branch (a): personally delivered to the defendant within New York City: it must appear and answer within 20 days after service, and service is complete on delivery. Branch (b): served any other way (substituted, nail-and-mail, mail under CPLR 312-a, outside the city under CCA 404): it must appear and answer within 30 days after proof of service is filed with the clerk, and service is complete on that filing (NY:CCA-410-service-complete). A default judgment is sought only after that time runs (and after the 3215(g)(3) 20-day mailing: NY:CPLR-3215(g)(3)).
proposed.quote: (a) If the summons is personally delivered to the defendant within the city of New York, it shall require him to appear and answer within twenty days after its service. (b) If the summons is served by any means other than personal delivery to the defendant within the city of New York, it shall provide that the defendant must appear and answer within thirty days after proof of service is filed with the clerk.

reason: A Civil Court summons is served as in Supreme Court (including mail under CPLR 312-a) but only within New York City unless a statute such as CCA 404 authorizes more; decides whether a tenant who has left the city can be served.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: The landlord serves a summons on a former tenant in a Civil Court action.
proposed.effect: Service follows Supreme Court practice (personal delivery, substituted service, affix-and-mail: NY:CPLR-308-natural-person; mail with acknowledgment: NY:CPLR-312-a-mail-service), but is made only within New York City unless another law authorizes service beyond the city. A tenant who has left the city is served outside it under CCA 404 on a claim arising from its possession of the NYC unit (NY:CCA-404-long-arm).
proposed.quote: Service of summons shall be made in the manner prescribed in supreme court practice, including the optional method of service by mail authorized by CPLR 312-a, but it shall be made only within the city of New York unless service beyond the city be authorized by this act or by such other provision of law, other than the CPLR, as expressly applies to courts of limited jurisdiction or to all courts of the state.

reason: Gives the Civil Court personal jurisdiction over a non-resident of the city on a claim arising from its possession or use of real property in the city, served anywhere; a former tenant who moved out of the city or state can be sued in NYC Civil Court for the balance, and a non-resident owner by the tenant.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: A party to a claim over the tenancy does not reside in New York City when suit is brought. Branch (a): the landlord sues a former tenant who moved out of the city or state. Branch (b): the tenant sues an owner who lives or is organized outside the city.
proposed.effect: The Civil Court has personal jurisdiction over a non-resident of the city (or its executor or administrator) on a cause of action arising from its transacting business in the city, contracting to supply goods or services there, committing a tortious act there (not defamation), or owning, using or possessing real property in the city, in person or by an agent. Branch (a): the former tenant's balance arises from its use and possession of the NYC unit, so it may be served outside the city and the state in any manner that would give the Supreme Court jurisdiction. Branch (b): the owner owns the NYC property, so the same applies. An appearance does not extend jurisdiction to unrelated claims. A corporation or association that cannot be served by personal delivery in the city is treated as a non-resident.
proposed.quote: (a) Acts which are the basis of jurisdiction. The court may exercise personal jurisdiction over any non-resident of the city of New York, or his executor or administrator, as to a cause of action arising from any of the acts enumerated in this section, in the same manner as if he were a domiciliary of the state and a resident of the city of New York if, in person or through an agent, he: 1. transacts any business within the city of New York or contracts anywhere to supply goods or services in the city of New York; or 2. commits a tortious act within the city of New York, except as to a cause of action for defamation of character arising from the act; or 3. owns, uses or possesses any real property situated within the city of New York. (b) Service of summons. Service of summons under this section may be made in such manner and at such place, regardless of city or state lines, as would confer jurisdiction on supreme court in a like case. (c) Effect of appearance. Where personal jurisdiction is based solely upon this section, an appearance does not confer such jurisdiction with respect to causes of action not arising from an act enumerated in this section. (d) Corporation or association. If service of the summons cannot be effected by personal delivery thereof within the city of New York so as to acquire in personam jurisdiction of a corporation or unincorporated association, such corporation or association shall be deemed a non-resident of the city of New York for purposes of this section.

reason: Out-of-city service without personal jurisdiction for real property, chattel, attachment and interpleader-deposit cases; a balance or deposit action against a moved-away party is reached with personal jurisdiction under CCA 404 instead.
Publication only in the CCA 405 in-rem cases, which do not include a balance or deposit action; publication against a natural person in a personal action is CPLR 315-316.

Proof of service must be filed with the Civil Court clerk by the marshal's or sheriff's certificate or the server's affidavit; the filing starts the tenant's 30-day answer time where service was not personal.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: The landlord has served the summons and complaint on a former tenant in a Civil Court action.
proposed.effect: Proof of service is filed with the clerk in the county of suit, by the certificate of the sheriff or marshal or the affidavit of the person who served. Where service was not personal delivery in the city, the tenant's time to answer runs 30 days from this filing (NY:CCA-402-answer-time).
proposed.quote: (a) Proof of service of the summons and complaint, notice of petition and petition or order to show cause and petition shall be filed with the clerk of the court in the county in which the action is brought. (b) Proof of service shall be made by the certificate of the sheriff or marshal or by the affidavit of the person by whom the service was made.

reason: Service of a Civil Court summons is complete on personal delivery, or otherwise on filing proof of service; this fixes the start of the answer period and default timing.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: The landlord serves a former tenant with a Civil Court summons.
proposed.effect: Service is complete immediately on personal delivery to the tenant within the city, or, for any other method, on the filing of proof of service (NY:CCA-409-proof-of-service).
proposed.quote: The service of summons is complete: (a) immediately upon personal delivery to the defendant, where § 402 (a) is applicable; or (b) upon the filing of proof of service, where § 402 (b) is applicable.

reason: The summons and complaint must be served within 120 days after filing or the action is dismissed without prejudice unless the court extends; a deadline whose miss can end a suit brought near the limitations date.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: A party has filed a summons and complaint (or third-party complaint) in NYC Civil Court over the tenancy.
proposed.effect: It must serve the defendant within 120 days after filing. If not, the court on motion dismisses the action without prejudice as to that defendant, or extends the time on good cause or in the interest of justice. A dismissal after the limitations period has run leaves only the CPLR 205(a) six-month recommencement where it applies (NY:CPLR-204-208-tolling).
proposed.quote: Service of the summons and complaint, third-party summons and complaint, petition with a notice of petition or order to show cause and petition shall be made within one hundred twenty days after the filing of the summons and complaint, third-party summons and complaint, or petition with notice of petition or order to show cause and petition, provided that if service is not made upon a defendant within the time provided in this section, the court, upon motion, shall dismiss the action without prejudice as to that defendant, or upon good cause shown or in the interest of justice, extend the time for service.

reason: The interest rule sets interest from each due date; 412 adds that where interest runs from the start of the action (for example a single intermediate date the court takes as commencement), it starts only when service is complete with the actual index number on the summons.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: In an NYC Civil Court case over the tenancy, interest is awarded from the date the action or proceeding began (rather than from each amount's due date under NY:CPLR-5001(a)-(b)).
proposed.effect: That interest does not begin to accrue until service is complete with the actual index number properly shown on the summons given to the party who must pay the interest. Interest computed from each amount's own due date is unaffected.
proposed.quote: In any action, petition, order to show cause or other proceeding wherein interest accrues from the date of the inception of the action, petition, order or proceeding, said entitlement to interest shall not begin to accrue until service is completed by the actual index number being properly depicted on the summons and provided to the party to be charged with the payment of interest.

reason: A Civil Court provisional remedy (such as attachment) runs only within New York City against persons or property there; limits pre-judgment attachment against a tenant who moved away.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: The landlord obtains a provisional remedy (attachment) out of the NYC Civil Court against a former tenant.
proposed.effect: Practice follows the CPLR, but the remedy is executed only within New York City against persons or property there, with returns to the Civil Court clerk; property outside the city is reached only through the Supreme Court.
proposed.quote: Whenever the remedies set forth in § 209 of this act may issue out of this court under the terms of said section, practice and procedure thereon shall be governed, insofar as consistent with this act, by the CPLR and such other provisions of law governing practice and procedure thereon in the supreme court, subject to the following: (a) The remedy may be executed only within the city of New York, against persons or property within the city of New York. (b) When a return is required, the return shall be made to the clerk of this court in the county out of which the remedy issued.

reason: Applies CPLR tender and offer-to-compromise rules (3219-3221) in Civil Court, with the added duty to file a copy with the clerk; changes how a landlord or tenant makes a cost-shifting settlement offer.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: A party to an NYC Civil Court case over the tenancy makes a written tender, a conditional offer to liquidate damages, or an offer to compromise (NY:CPLR-3219-tender, NY:CPLR-3221-offer-to-compromise).
proposed.effect: The CPLR rules apply, and a copy of the tender, offer or notice must be filed with the clerk when it is served on the other party.
proposed.quote: The provisions of Rules 3219, 3220 and 3221 of the CPLR, treating respectively of tender, offer to liquidate damages conditionally and offer to compromise, shall be applicable in this court, with the additional requirement that at the time of service upon the other party of the "written tender", "written offer" or "written notice", as referred to in said rules, a copy of such tender, offer or notice shall be filed with the clerk.

reason: In Civil Court a money-only claim may be pleaded by an endorsement on the summons (nature, substance and default amount); a formal complaint is served with the summons; changes what the landlord must serve to commence.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: The landlord sues a former tenant in the NYC Civil Court for money only.
proposed.effect: Pleadings are formal as in Supreme Court, except that the claim may be stated by an endorsement on the summons giving the nature and substance of the claim and the amount for which judgment will be taken on default (by the clerk if the landlord has no attorney); a tenant appearing without an attorney may state its answer to the clerk. A formal complaint, if used, is served with the summons. The court may at any time direct a formal pleading. The pending S9760 would require the complaint, with the lease attached, served with the summons (NY:S9760-pleading-service).
proposed.quote: (a) All pleadings shall be formal pleadings, as in supreme court practice, except that: (1) If the plaintiff's cause of action is for money only, the cause of action may be set forth by indorsement upon the summons. The indorsement shall consist of a statement of the nature and substance of the cause of action, and the summons in such instance shall set forth the amount in which the plaintiff will take judgment in the event of default. If the plaintiff shall appear without attorney, such indorsement shall be made by the clerk. (2) Where the plaintiff's cause of action is for money only and the defendant appears without attorney, he may describe his answer to the clerk, who shall indorse the nature and substance of the answer on, or annex it to, the summons. (b) If a formal complaint must be or is used, it shall be served with the summons, except that if service is made by publication the CPLR shall govern. (c) The address of the defendant, and that of his attorney if he shall appear by attorney, shall be stated with or in the answer. (d) The rules may provide, in actions for money only in designated categories in which a party might otherwise proceed by indorsement as above provided, that a formal complaint, or a formal answer, or both, shall be required. (e) The court in any case may, at any time before judgment, on its own motion or on the motion on notice of a party, direct the service and filing of a formal pleading.

reason: Lets the court hear legal or equitable defenses; it adds no step, amount or deadline for either side.
In Civil Court a plaintiff need not reply to a counterclaim, which is deemed denied; a landlord suing for the balance is not defaulted on the tenant's deposit counterclaim by not replying.

proposed.instrument: New York City Civil Court Act
proposed.condition: The former tenant answers the landlord's Civil Court balance action with a counterclaim (for example for the deposit or double damages), or the reverse.
proposed.effect: The plaintiff need not reply unless the court orders; a voluntary reply is due within 10 days after service of the answer; without a reply the counterclaim's allegations are deemed denied, so no default arises on it.
proposed.quote: (a) Counterclaim. The plaintiff may reply to a counterclaim but shall not be required to do so except by court order. If the plaintiff elects voluntarily to reply, he shall do so within ten days after service of the answer containing the counterclaim. In the absence of a reply the allegations of the counterclaim shall be deemed denied by the plaintiff.

reason: Verification of Civil Court pleadings follows the CPLR; verification form changes no step in the chain (default proof is CPLR 3215(f)).

Amending pleadings in a pending Civil Court case; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline or precondition in the settlement or the decision to sue (relation back is at CPLR 203(f)).

Makes the CPLR simplified procedure (a voluntary submission of an agreed controversy without pleadings) available in Civil Court; a litigation-format option that changes no amount, deadline or precondition.

The court's standard for compelling joinder of absent parties; who may be sued alone on a joint lease obligation is CPLR 1501-1502, and who is paid a joint refund is NY:ADJ-cotenants-payee. It adds no step to the settlement.

A pending action continues after a transfer of interest unless the court substitutes the transferee; who owns a pre-sale balance is decided by NY:RPL-223 and assignment limits by NY:JUD-489-champerty.

The parties rule states substitution on death; 1021 adds that substitution must be sought within a reasonable time or the action may be dismissed (not on the merits), and that on a party's death the court orders the estate's interested persons to show cause.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: A party to a pending action over the tenancy dies (for example the former tenant sued for the balance) or another event requires substitution.
proposed.effect: Substitution is moved by the successors or representatives or by any party; a person who should be substituted and does not appear may be made a defendant. If the event occurs before final judgment and substitution is not made within a reasonable time, the action may be dismissed as to that party, not on the merits unless the court says so. On a party's death without timely substitution, the court, before proceeding, orders the persons interested in the estate to show cause why the action should not be dismissed. Operator step: when a sued former tenant dies, seek appointment of a fiduciary and substitution promptly (claims against the estate: NY:ADJ-tenant-death-payee).
judgment_terms: reasonable time
proposed.quote: A motion for substitution may be made by the successors or representatives of a party or by any party. If a person who should be substituted does not appear voluntarily he may be made a party defendant. If the event requiring substitution occurs before final judgment and substitution is not made within a reasonable time, the action may be dismissed as to the party for whom substitution should have been made, however, such dismissal shall not be on the merits unless the court shall so indicate. If the event requiring substitution occurs after final judgment, substitution may be made in either the court from or to which an appeal could be or is taken, or the court of original instance, and if substitution is not made within four months after the event requiring substitution, the court to which the appeal is or could be taken may dismiss the appeal, impose conditions or prevent it from being taken. Whether or not it occurs before or after final judgment, if the event requiring substitution is the death of a party, and timely substitution has not been made, the court, before proceeding further, shall, on such notice as it may in its discretion direct, order the persons interested in the decedent’s estate to show cause why the action or appeal should not be dismissed.

reason: Extends in-suit procedural deadlines until 15 days after substitution; litigation mechanics that change no step, amount or precondition of the settlement.
A civil claim is not merged in a criminal prosecution for the same act; the landlord's damage claim survives any prosecution without any step by the landlord.

The parties rule bars a default against an infant or adjudicated incompetent; 1201 adds who appears for them and that an adult incapable of defending its rights appears by a guardian ad litem, which the landlord must obtain before pursuing an incapacitated former tenant.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.actor: landlord (plaintiff); representative of the former tenant
proposed.condition: The landlord sues a former tenant who is an infant, a person judicially declared incompetent, a conservatee, or an adult incapable of adequately prosecuting or defending its rights (or such a person sues the landlord for the deposit).
proposed.effect: An infant appears by the guardian of its property, else a parent with legal custody, else another custodian, or, if married, an adult spouse living with it; an adjudicated incompetent appears by the committee of its property; a conservatee by the conservator. A guardian ad litem appears where there is no such representative, where the court so directs for conflict or other cause, or for an adult incapable of adequately prosecuting or defending its rights. The landlord seeks a guardian ad litem (CPLR 1202) before pursuing default against such a tenant (NY:CPLR-1203-1015-5208-parties).
judgment_terms: adult incapable of adequately prosecuting or defending his rights
proposed.quote: Unless the court appoints a guardian ad litem, an infant shall appear by the guardian of his property or, if there is no such guardian, by a parent having legal custody, or, if there is no such parent, by another person or agency having legal custody, or, if the infant is married, by an adult spouse residing with the infant, a person judicially declared to be incompetent shall appear by the committee of his property, and a conservatee shall appear by the conservator of his property. A person shall appear by his guardian ad litem if he is an infant and has no guardian of his property, parent, or other person or agency having legal custody, or adult spouse with whom he resides, or if he is an infant, person judicially declared to be incompetent, or a conservatee as defined in section 77.01 of the mental hygiene law and the court so directs because of a conflict of interest or for other cause, or if he is an adult incapable of adequately prosecuting or defending his rights.

reason: An infant, incompetent, conservatee or guardian-ad-litem-represented former tenant (or its representative) is not liable for costs unless the court orders; changes the landlord's recoverable costs against such a tenant.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: The landlord obtains judgment against a former tenant who is an infant, adjudicated incompetent, conservatee or represented by a guardian ad litem, or against its representative.
proposed.effect: Neither the tenant nor its representative is liable for costs unless the court orders otherwise; the judgment carries the principal and interest, and costs only by order.
proposed.quote: An infant, a person judicially declared to be incompetent, a conservatee, a person for whom a guardian ad litem has been appointed, or a representative of any such person, shall not be liable for costs unless the court otherwise orders.

reason: On a joint lease obligation the landlord may proceed against the co-tenants it has served and take judgment against all named; changes how a balance owed by co-tenants (one unreachable) is pursued.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: The landlord sues co-tenants (or a tenant and a guarantor) on a joint lease obligation and serves fewer than all of them.
proposed.effect: It may proceed against those served unless the court directs otherwise, and a judgment for it may be taken against all the named defendants; the judgment reaches the unserved co-obligor's individually held property only through a later action under NY:CPLR-1502-later-action-co-obligor. Liability that is joint and several under the lease may instead be pursued against any one co-tenant alone.
proposed.quote: Where less than all of the named defendants in an action based upon a joint obligation, contract or liability are served with the summons, the plaintiff may proceed against the defendants served, unless the court otherwise directs, and if the judgment is for the plaintiff it may be taken against all the defendants.

reason: To reach an unserved co-tenant's own property after a joint judgment, the landlord must bring a second, verified action, in which the co-tenant keeps all its defenses; decides whether pursuing an absent co-tenant is worth it.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: The landlord holds a judgment on a joint lease obligation taken against all co-tenants under CPLR 1501, and a co-tenant was not served in that action.
proposed.effect: To obtain a judgment enforceable against that co-tenant's individually held property for the unpaid remainder, the landlord brings a later action with a verified complaint, treated as based on the same obligation for provisional remedies. The co-tenant may raise every defense and counterclaim it could have raised in the first action (for example its share of the deposit or wear and tear), objections to the first judgment, and defenses arising since.
proposed.quote: A subsequent action against a co-obligor who was not summoned in the original action must be maintained in order to procure a judgment enforceable against his individually held property for the sum remaining unpaid upon the original judgment, and such action shall be regarded as based upon the same obligation, contract or liability as the original judgment for the purpose of obtaining any provisional remedy. The complaint in the subsequent action shall be verified. The defendant in the subsequent action may raise any defenses or counterclaims that he might have raised in the original action if the summons had been served on him when it was first served on a co-obligor, and may raise objections to the original judgment, and defenses or counterclaims that have arisen since it was entered.

reason: Lets the court correct or disregard filing mistakes in a pending case; in-suit discretion that changes no step, amount or deadline of the settlement.

Lets the court set aside a judicial sale within a year for defective notice or manner; it binds the enforcement officer's sale and changes no step or amount in the landlord's settlement or collection decision.
General judicial power to extend times set by statute or rule, except where the law expressly bars it (limitations periods cannot be extended: CPLR 201); it fixes no step or deadline of its own.
Allows a court to excuse law-office failure on a motion to vacate a default; court discretion inside CPLR 5015 and 3012(d), adding no step or deadline.

The limitation rules state the periods; 201 adds that a shorter period may be set by written agreement and that no court may extend a limitation period. A lease clause shortening the tenant's time to sue over the deposit is void under GOL 7-108's anti-waiver clause.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: A lease or other written agreement between the landlord and the tenant sets a period for suing shorter than the statutory one. Branch (a): the clause limits the tenant's claims over the security deposit (return, forfeiture, double damages). Branch (b): the clause limits another claim between them (the landlord's balance, a tenant's non-deposit claim).
proposed.effect: Every action must be begun within the statutory period unless a different period is prescribed by law or a shorter one by written agreement, and no court may extend a period fixed by law. Branch (a): the clause is void, because GOL 7-108 makes absolutely void any agreement by a tenant waiving or modifying its rights under that section, and a shortened time to enforce them modifies them (and GOL 7-103(3) voids any waiver of the trust section); the statutory periods of NY:ADJ-tenant-deposit-claim-limitations apply. Branch (b): the clause is enforced if the shortened period is reasonable. A promise to extend the period is governed by NY:GOL-17-103-limitations-promise.
judgment_terms: reasonable shortened period
proposed.quote: An action, including one brought in the name or for the benefit of the state, must be commenced within the time specified in this article unless a different time is prescribed by law or a shorter time is prescribed by written agreement. No court shall extend the time limited by law for the commencement of an action.

construction.quote: Any agreement by a lessee or tenant of a dwelling waiving or modifying his rights as set forth in this section shall be absolutely void.

proposed.reasoning: CPLR 201 permits a shorter period by written agreement, but a specific statute voiding any agreement that modifies a tenant's deposit rights controls over the general permission for those rights; the remedy provisions of 7-108(1-a)(g) are rights set forth in the section.

reason: The borrowing statute: where a claim over the tenancy accrues outside New York in favor of a non-resident (an owner entity based out of state, a tenant who moved away before its claim accrued), the shorter of New York's and that place's period applies. Can bar the landlord's balance suit or the tenant's deposit suit early.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: A claim between the landlord and a former tenant is for economic loss (unpaid rent or damage; the deposit wrongly kept). Branch (a): the plaintiff is a New York resident when the claim accrues (an individual owner domiciled here; an entity with its principal place of business here; a tenant still living here). Branch (b): the plaintiff resides outside New York when the claim accrues (an owner entity organized and based elsewhere; a tenant who had moved out of state by the end of the 14 days).
proposed.effect: An economic-loss claim accrues where the plaintiff resides and sustains the economic impact (Global Fin. Corp. v Triarc Corp., 93 NY2d 525 [1999]). Branch (a): New York's period alone applies (NY:CPLR-213(2), NY:ADJ-tenant-deposit-claim-limitations). Branch (b): the action must be timely under both New York's period and the period of the place where the plaintiff resided, including that place's tolling rules; the shorter controls, and a lease choice-of-law clause does not change this. An assignee or collector suing on the owner's claim stands in the owner's position (Portfolio Recovery Assoc., LLC v King, 14 NY3d 410 [2010]). Operator step: record the owner's place of residence (for an entity, where it sustains the loss, its principal place of business) and the tenant's residence at accrual.
judgment_terms: place where the plaintiff resides and sustains the economic impact of the loss
proposed.quote: An action based upon a cause of action accruing without the state cannot be commenced after the expiration of the time limited by the laws of either the state or the place without the state where the cause of action accrued, except that where the cause of action accrued in favor of a resident of the state the time limited by the laws of the state shall apply.

reason: Recommencement rules only for actions on instruments under CPLR 213(4) (mortgages and other real-property secured instruments); a lease balance or deposit claim is not one (its recommencement is CPLR 205(a), stated).

Where a lease makes a sum payable only on the landlord's demand, the period runs from when the landlord could first demand, not from the demand; a deposit held as trust money is not a 'special demand' deposit. Fixes accrual of such charges.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: Computing when a claim between the landlord and a former tenant accrued. Branch (a): the lease makes a charge (for example repair costs) payable on the landlord's demand or bill. Branch (b): the tenant's claim to the deposit. Branch (c): the parties' account.
proposed.effect: Branch (a): where a demand is necessary to sue, the period runs from when the right to make the demand was complete (when the costs were incurred and billable), not from when the landlord chose to demand; delaying the bill does not extend the period. Branch (b): the deposit is repayable by statute within 14 days after vacating without any demand, so its period runs from the end of the 14 days (NY:ADJ-tenant-deposit-claim-limitations); the special-demand and fiduciary-discovery rules of 206(a)(1)-(2) do not move it. Branch (c): a rent ledger of charges and payments is not a mutual, open and current account with reciprocal demands, so the 'last transaction' rule of 206(d) does not apply; each rent installment accrues on its due date (a part payment's effect: NY:GOL-17-101-acknowledgment).
proposed.quote: (a) Where demand necessary. Except as provided in article 3 of the uniform commercial code, where a demand is necessary to entitle a person to commence an action, the time within which the action must be commenced shall be computed from the time when the right to make the demand is complete, except that 1. where a right grows out of the receipt or detention of money or property by a trustee, agent, attorney or other person acting in a fiduciary capacity, the time within which the action must be commenced shall be computed from the time when the person having the right to make the demand discovered the facts upon which the right depends; and 2. where there was a deposit of money to be repaid only upon a special demand, or a delivery of personal property not to be returned specifically or in kind at a fixed time or upon a fixed contingency, the time within which the action must be commenced shall be computed from the demand for repayment or return. (b) Based on misconduct of agent. Where a judgment is entered against a principal in an action based upon an injury resulting from the act or omission of his deputy or agent, the time within which an action by the principal against the deputy or agent to recover damages by reason of such judgment must be commenced shall be computed, from the time when the action against the principal was finally determined. Where an injury results from the representation by a person that he is an agent with authority to execute a contract in behalf of a principal, the time within which an action to recover damages for breach of warranty of authority must be commenced by the person injured against the purported agent shall be computed from the time the person injured discovered the facts constituting lack of authority. (c) Based on breach of covenant of seizin or against incumbrances. In an action based upon breach of a covenant of seizin or against incumbrances, the time within which the action must be commenced shall be computed from an eviction. (d) Based on account. In an action based upon a mutual, open and current account, where there have been reciprocal demands between the parties, the time within which the action must be commenced shall be computed from the time of the last transaction in the account on either side.

reason: Tolls limitation periods while a party cannot sue because of a war between the United States and the country where it resides or of which it is a national; applies to a former tenant or owner in such a country.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: A party to a claim over the tenancy is a national of, or resides or sojourns in, a foreign country at war with the United States or its allies (or territory it occupies).
proposed.effect: The time from the start of the war to the end of hostilities (for a national who cannot sue), or the period of residence or sojourn there during the war (for a claimant living there), is not counted in the limitation period.
proposed.quote: (b) Right of noncitizen. Where a person is unable to commence an action in the courts of the state because any party is a noncitizen subject or citizen of a foreign country at war with the United States or any of its allies, whether the cause of action accrued during or prior to the war, the time which elapsed between the commencement of the war and the termination of hostilities with such country is not a part of the time within which the action must be commenced.

reason: How papers are served between parties after an action is begun (on the attorney, by mail with five added days, fax, overnight, electronic); in-suit mechanics that change no settlement step. Commencement service is CPLR 308-312-a and CCA 403.

A court may let a party keep its address confidential for safety, and the address of a domestic-violence program resident is never revealed; changes how a landlord serves and pursues a former tenant who is a domestic-violence victim.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.actor: landlord (plaintiff) and its collector; former tenant
proposed.condition: The landlord sues, or is sued by, a former tenant whose address the court orders kept confidential because disclosure would pose an unreasonable risk to its health or safety, or who lives or lived in a residential program for domestic-violence victims.
proposed.effect: The court may authorize the tenant to keep its residential and business addresses and telephone numbers out of papers, sealed pending the finding, and designates the clerk or another disinterested person as agent for service, who forwards process; the landlord serves through that agent. The present address of a domestic-violence program resident, and the program's address, are not revealed by the court. The tenant keeps the agent informed of address changes. Operator step: where a former tenant ended the lease as a domestic-violence victim (NY:RPL-227-c(1)), do not seek or publish its new address in court papers; use the designated agent.
proposed.quote: (a) Notwithstanding any other provision of law, in any civil proceeding, whether or not an order of protection or temporary order of protection is sought or has been sought in the past, the court may, upon its own motion or upon the motion of any party, authorize any party to keep his or her residential and business addresses and telephone numbers confidential from any party in any pleadings or other papers submitted to the court, where the court makes specific findings on the record supporting a conclusion that disclosure of such addresses or telephone numbers would pose an unreasonable risk to the health or safety of a party. Pending such a finding, any such addresses or telephone numbers of the party seeking confidentiality shall be safeguarded and sealed in order to prevent its inadvertent or unauthorized use or disclosure. (b) Notwithstanding any other provision of law, if a party has resided or resides in a residential program for victims of domestic violence as defined in section four hundred fifty-nine-a of the social services law, the present address of such party and the address of the residential program for victims of domestic violence shall not be revealed by the court or any court personnel who may have access to such information. (c) Upon such authorization, the court shall designate the clerk of the court or such other disinterested person as it deems appropriate, with consent of such disinterested person, as the agent for service of process for the party whose residential and business addresses or telephone numbers are to remain confidential and shall notify the parties of such designation and the address of the agent in writing. The clerk or disinterested person designated by the court shall, when served with process on behalf of the party whose information is to remain confidential, promptly notify such party whose information is to remain confidential and forward such process to him or her in a manner calculated to be timely received. (d) In any case in which such confidentiality authorization is made, the party whose information is to remain confidential shall inform the clerk of the court or disinterested person designated by the court of any change in address for purposes of receipt of service of process or any papers.

reason: A settlement with a former tenant in a pending case binds only if in a writing signed by the party or its attorney, made in open court, or so-ordered, and its terms are filed by the defendant with the county clerk; decides whether a settlement is enforceable.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: The landlord and a former tenant agree to settle or otherwise resolve a pending action or proceeding over the tenancy (a payment plan, a reduced balance, return of part of the deposit).
proposed.effect: The agreement binds a party only if it is in a writing signed by that party or its attorney, made between counsel in open court, or reduced to an order and entered; an oral out-of-court settlement is not binding. The defendant files the terms of a stipulation of settlement with the county clerk. Payment on a settled deposit claim: NY:CPLR-5003-a-settlement-payment.
proposed.quote: An agreement between parties or their attorneys relating to any matter in an action, other than one made between counsel in open court, is not binding upon a party unless it is in a writing subscribed by him or his attorney or reduced to the form of an order and entered. With respect to stipulations of settlement and notwithstanding the form of the stipulation of settlement, the terms of such stipulation shall be filed by the defendant with the county clerk.

reason: Residential rent overcharge claims arise only for rent-stabilized or rent-controlled units (regulated rent); out of aperture for a market-rate unit (Review 2).
Discovery accrual for injury from latent exposure to substances (toxic torts); no claim in the settlement chain is of that kind.

Where one person sues for a contract sum and another claims the same sum but cannot be served, the defendant may notify the other claimant and cut its time to sue to one year; a tool for a landlord facing competing claims to a deposit refund.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: A former tenant (or its estate, trustee or co-tenant) sues the landlord for the deposit refund over $50, and another person who cannot be served within the court's jurisdiction claims the same sum (for example an absent co-tenant, or a person claiming as the tenant's agent).
proposed.effect: Within 20 days after service of the complaint or receipt of the adverse claim, whichever is later, the landlord may move for an order permitting notice to the absent claimant; the court grants it if the claim exists, the action is not collusive and the claimant cannot be served. Notice is sent by registered mail with the summons, complaint and order to the claimant's last known address; proof of mailing is filed within 10 days of the order or the order lapses, and notice is deemed given on the tenth day after the order. The claimant must then sue within one year after notice (never longer than its own period). The court stays the action up to one year, may require the landlord to post an undertaking, and vacates the stay if the claimant intervenes or sues.
proposed.quote: (a) Action to recover money. 1. No action for the recovery of any sum of money due and payable under or on account of a contract, or for any part thereof, shall be commenced by any person who has made claim to the sum, after the expiration of one year from the giving of notice, as hereinafter provided, to the claimant that an action commenced by another person is pending to recover the sum, or any part thereof, exceeding fifty dollars in amount. This limitation shall not be construed to enlarge the time within which the cause of action of the claimant would otherwise be barred. 2. If any person shall make claim for the recovery of any sum of money due and payable under or on account of a contract, and an action has theretofore been, or shall thereafter be, commenced by another person to recover the sum, or any part thereof, exceeding fifty dollars in amount, the defendant in such action may, within twenty days from the date of service upon him of the complaint or from the date of receipt by him of the claim, whichever occurs later, make a motion before the court in which the action is pending for an order permitting the defendant to give notice to the claimant that the action is pending. The court in which the action is pending shall grant the order where it appears that a person not a party to the action has made claim against the defendant for the sum of money, or any part thereof, exceeding fifty dollars in amount; that the action was brought without collusion between the defendant and the plaintiff; and that the claimant cannot, with due diligence, be served with process in such a manner as to obtain jurisdiction over his person. The order shall provide, among such other terms and conditions as justice may require, that notice shall be given to the claimant by sending by registered mail a copy of the summons and complaint in the action and the order and a notice addressed to the claimant at his last known address. In the event that registration of mail directed to any country or part thereof shall be discontinued or suspended, notice to a claimant whose last known address is within such country or part thereof shall be given by ordinary mail, under such terms and conditions as the court may direct. Proof that the notice has been mailed shall be filed within ten days from the date of the order; otherwise the order becomes inoperative. Upon such filing, notice shall be deemed to have been given on the tenth day after the date of such order. 3. Upon proof by affidavit or otherwise, to the satisfaction of the court, that the conditions of this subdivision have been satisfied and that there is no collusion between the claimant and the defendant, the court shall make an order staying further prosecution of the action for a period not to exceed one year from the date when the notice shall have been given to the claimant. At the time of the granting of such order or at any time thereafter, the court, upon the motion of any party, shall, as a condition of the granting of the order or its continuation, impose upon the defendant such terms as justice may require as to the furnishing of an undertaking in an amount to be fixed by the court. The stay shall be vacated and the undertaking, if any has been given, may be discharged or modified, as justice may require, upon proof to the court by any party to the action that the claimant has intervened or has instituted another action in any court of this state to recover the said sum of money, or any part thereof, exceeding fifty dollars. 4. A motion for any relief as prescribed in this subdivision shall be made on notice to all other parties to the action. 5. Whenever claims are made by two or more persons, each claiming to be, to the exclusion of the other, the duly authorized deputy, officer or agent to demand, receive, collect, sue for or recover the same sum of money due and payable under or on account of a contract, or any part thereof, exceeding fifty dollars in amount, for and on behalf of the same person, each person making such a claim shall be deemed an adverse claimant. Notwithstanding that an action has been commenced in the name of or on behalf of the person for whom he claims to be the duly authorized deputy, officer or agent, any such adverse claimant may be notified of the pendency of an action as provided in this subdivision and may intervene in the action and be designated as claiming to be or as the alleged deputy, officer or agent. 6. Whenever an action has been commenced for the recovery of any sum of money exceeding fifty dollars due and payable under or on account of a contract and the records of the defendant show that a person other than the plaintiff has the right, exclusive of other deputies, officers or agents of the plaintiff, to demand, sue for and recover the same sum of money, or any part thereof, exceeding fifty dollars in amount, either in his own name, on his own behalf, or as the authorized deputy, officer or agent for the plaintiff, and the defendant has received no notice of transfer, revocation, or other change in right or authority acceptable to it, the person so appearing on the records shall be deemed to have made an adverse claim to the sum of money and may be treated as an adverse claimant.

reason: Notice of claim and a one-year-ninety-day limit for actions against public entities; no party to a market-rate tenancy settlement is one.
Transitional rules for claims that accrued before CPLR article 2 took effect in 1963; no current claim is affected.
General power of a court to stay a pending action; the effect of a stay on limitations is stated at NY:CPLR-204-208-tolling and bankruptcy and military stays elsewhere. It adds no step.

On request the clerk dockets an order directing payment of money (including motion costs, a so-ordered payment) as a judgment, making it enforceable and interest-bearing; a step for enforcing a court-ordered payment from a former tenant.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: A court order in a case over the tenancy directs a party to pay money (for example motion costs, or payment under a so-ordered settlement).
proposed.effect: At a party's request the clerk dockets the order as a judgment; it then bears interest from docketing (NY:CPLR-5003-judgment-interest) and is enforced as a money judgment.
proposed.quote: At the request of any party the clerk shall docket as a judgment an order directing the payment of money, including motion costs,

reason: Suing one co-tenant or the guarantor, or holding an unsatisfied judgment against one, does not bar an action against the others; and a tenant may sue either the managing agent or the undisclosed owner. Changes whom the balance or deposit claim may be pursued against.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: Branch (a): several persons are liable for the balance (co-tenants, a guarantor). Branch (b): the lease was made by a managing agent for an owner the tenant did not know, and the tenant has a claim (for example for the deposit).
proposed.effect: Branch (a): starting or pursuing an action against one, or recovering an unsatisfied judgment against one, is not an election that bars an action against the others (releases: NY:GOL-15-104-105-cotenant-release). Branch (b): after the principal is disclosed, suing either the agent or the principal, or an unsatisfied judgment against either, does not bar an action against the other.
proposed.quote: (a) Action against several persons. Where causes of action exist against several persons, the commencement or maintenance of an action against one, or the recovery against one of a judgment which is unsatisfied, shall not be deemed an election of remedies which bars an action against the others. (b) Action against agent and undisclosed principal. Where causes of action exist against an agent and his undisclosed principal, the commencement or maintenance, after disclosure of the principal, of an action against either, or the recovery of a judgment against either which is unsatisfied, shall not be deemed an election of remedies which bars an action against the other.

reason: Rescission of a transaction void or voidable for fraud, mistake, duress or incapacity without tendering back benefits first; rescinding a lease is not a step in settling the account of a tenancy that has ended.

Removes the fact/law distinction when a court grants relief for mistake; whether a sum a tenant paid is refundable or credited is decided by the charge rules themselves (for example NY:RPL-238-a(1)-no-move-in-fees, NY:ADJ-no-fee-retention), so it adds no step to the account.
Certificate of merit in residential mortgage foreclosure of a home loan; not a landlord-tenant claim.
Pleading form for the demand for relief; the limit of a default judgment to the amount demanded is CPLR 3215(b). It adds no step in the chain.

Defenses such as the statute of limitations, payment, release, bankruptcy discharge and res judicata must be pleaded or are lost; changes what the landlord (defending a deposit suit) or the tenant (defending a balance suit) must raise.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: A party answers a claim over the tenancy (the landlord answering a deposit suit; the tenant answering a balance suit).
proposed.effect: It denies statements it knows or believes untrue and states lack of knowledge where it lacks it; other statements are deemed admitted. It pleads every matter that would otherwise surprise the other side, including arbitration and award, collateral estoppel, discharge in bankruptcy, illegality, fraud, infancy or other disability, payment, release, res judicata, statute of frauds and statute of limitations; a defense not pleaded (or raised by timely motion) is waived. Operator step: when the landlord is sued, put the limitations defense, payment, any signed release and the small-claims preclusion (NY:CCA-1808-preclusion) in the answer.
proposed.quote: (a) Denials. A party shall deny those statements known or believed by him to be untrue. He shall specify those statements as to the truth of which he lacks knowledge or information sufficient to form a belief and this shall have the effect of a denial. All other statements of a pleading are deemed admitted, except that where no responsive pleading is permitted they are deemed denied or avoided. (b) Affirmative defenses. A party shall plead all matters which if not pleaded would be likely to take the adverse party by surprise or would raise issues of fact not appearing on the face of a prior pleading such as arbitration and award, collateral estoppel, culpable conduct claimed in diminution of damages as set forth in article fourteen-A, discharge in bankruptcy, facts showing illegality either by statute or common law, fraud, infancy or other disability of the party defending, payment, release, res judicata, statute of frauds, or statute of limitation. The application of this subdivision shall not be confined to the instances enumerated.

reason: Says who may verify the landlord's pleading: the owner, an officer of a domestic corporation, or an agent (managing agent) where the owner is a foreign entity or out of county or the facts are within the agent's personal knowledge; decides whether the manager can sign the verification.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.actor: landlord, its officer or managing agent
proposed.condition: The landlord's complaint against a former tenant (or its answer to a deposit suit) is verified, for example so it can serve as proof on a default.
proposed.effect: A verification is a statement affirmed under penalty of perjury that the pleading is true to the deponent's knowledge except matters on information and belief. It is made by the party; for a domestic corporation, by an officer. It may be made by an agent (the managing agent) or the attorney where the party is a foreign corporation, is not in the county where the attorney has its office, where the claim is founded on a written instrument for the payment of money only in the agent's or attorney's possession, or where all material allegations are within the agent's or attorney's personal knowledge. Once a pleading is verified, later pleadings must be verified too. A defense not involving the merits must be verified.
proposed.quote: (a) Generally. A verification is a statement, subscribed and affirmed to be true under the penalties of perjury in accordance with rule twenty-one hundred six of this chapter, that the pleading is true to the knowledge of the deponent, except as to matters alleged on information and belief, and that as to those matters such deponent believes it to be true. Unless otherwise specified by law, where a pleading is verified, each subsequent pleading shall also be verified, except the answer of an infant and except as to matter in the pleading concerning which the party would be privileged from testifying as a witness. Where the complaint is not verified, a counterclaim, cross-claim or third-party claim in the answer may be separately verified in the same manner and with the same effect as if it were a separate pleading. (b) When answer must be verified. An answer shall be verified: 1. when the complaint charges the defendant with having confessed or suffered a judgment, executed a conveyance, assignment or other instrument, or transferred or delivered money or personal property with intent to hinder, delay or defraud his creditors, or with being a party or privy to such a transaction by another person with like intent towards the creditors of that person, or with any fraud whatever affecting a right or the property of another; or 2. in an action against a corporation to recover damages for the non-payment of a promissory note or other evidence of debt for the absolute payment of money upon demand or at a particular time. (c) Defense not involving the merits. A defense which does not involve the merits of the action shall be verified. (d) By whom verification made. The verification of a pleading shall be made by the affidavit of the party, or, if two or more parties united in interest are pleading together, by at least one of them who is acquainted with the facts, except: 1. if the party is a domestic corporation, the verification shall be made by an officer thereof and shall be deemed a verification by the party; 2. if the party is the state, a governmental subdivision, board, commission, or agency, or a public officer in behalf of any of them, the verification may be made by any person acquainted with the facts; and 3. if the party is a foreign corporation, or is not in the county where the attorney has his office, or if there are two or more parties united in interest and pleading together and none of them acquainted with the facts is within that county, or if the action or defense is founded upon a written instrument for the payment of money only which is in the possession of an agent or the attorney, or if all the material allegations of the pleading are within the personal knowledge of an agent or the attorney, the verification may be made by such agent or attorney.

reason: Treats a defectively verified pleading as unverified and lets the opponent reject it on prompt notice; in-suit pleading mechanics with no settlement consequence.
Amending pleadings in a pending action; in-suit mechanics (relation back of an amended claim for limitations is stated at CPLR 203(f)).
Pleadings are construed liberally; a canon for the court that adds no step or amount.

A party beyond New York's jurisdiction who sues here (a moved-away tenant suing for the deposit) designates its attorney, or the clerk, as agent to be served in the landlord's separate action on a claim that could have been a counterclaim; changes how the landlord can reach that tenant.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: A former tenant who is not otherwise subject to personal jurisdiction in New York sues the landlord in a New York court (for example over the deposit), and the landlord wants to sue it separately for the balance.
proposed.effect: While the tenant's action is pending, its attorney in that action (or the clerk if it has none) is its agent for service of a summons under CPLR 308 in the landlord's separate action, if that action could have been a counterclaim in the Supreme Court.
proposed.quote: The commencement of an action in the state by a person not subject to personal jurisdiction is a designation by him of his attorney appearing in the action or of the clerk of the court if no attorney appears, as agent, during the pendency of the action, for service of a summons pursuant to section 308, in any separate action in which such a person is a defendant and another party to the action is a plaintiff if such separate action would have been permitted as a counterclaim had the action been brought in the supreme court.

reason: Voluntary simplified procedure by a statement signed by all parties; a litigation-format option that changes no amount, deadline or precondition.
Enforces written contracts to use the simplified procedure; it concerns the forum format of a dispute both sides agreed to and changes no amount, deadline or precondition of the settlement.
How the court runs a simplified-procedure case (evidence rules relaxed, experts, default for failure to serve a statement); in-suit mechanics of a voluntary format.
Appeals in simplified-procedure cases; appellate practice.

Sets what the proof of service must show (papers, person, date, time, address, manner, a physical description of the person served, and the prior attempts for nail-and-mail); a defective affidavit exposes a default judgment to vacatur.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: The landlord serves a summons on a former tenant and files proof of service.
proposed.effect: The proof states the papers served, the person served, the date, time, address (or place) and manner of service, and facts showing an authorized person served in an authorized manner. For delivery to an individual it describes the person (gender, race, hair color, approximate age, weight, height, other features). For affix-and-mail service it states the dates, addresses and times of the earlier attempts at personal and substituted service. It is a sheriff's or marshal's certificate, a server's affidavit, or the signed CPLR 312-a acknowledgment; a written admission of service by the tenant also suffices.
proposed.quote: (a) Generally. Proof of service shall specify the papers served, the person who was served and the date, time, address, or, in the event there is no address, place and manner of service, and set forth facts showing that the service was made by an authorized person and in an authorized manner. (b) Personal service. Whenever service is made pursuant to this article by delivery of the summons to an individual, proof of service shall also include, in addition to any other requirement, a description of the person to whom it was so delivered, including, but not limited to, the process server’s perception of the person’s: gender, race, hair color, approximate age, approximate weight and height, and other identifying features. (c) Other service. Where service is made pursuant to subdivision four of section three hundred eight of this chapter, proof of service shall also specify the dates, addresses and the times of attempted service pursuant to subdivisions one, two or three of such section. (d) Form. Proof of service shall be in the form of a certificate if the service is made by a sheriff or other authorized public officer, in the form of an affidavit if made by any other person, or in the form of a signed acknowledgement of receipt of a summons and complaint, or summons and notice or notice of petition as provided for in section 312-a of this article. (e) Admission of service. A writing admitting service by the person to be served is adequate proof of service.

reason: In Supreme Court the summons must be served within 120 days after filing or the action is dismissed without prejudice unless extended; a deadline whose miss can end a claim filed near the limitations date.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: A party has commenced an action over the tenancy by filing in the Supreme Court (or another court applying CPLR 306-b).
proposed.effect: It must serve the summons and complaint (or summons with notice) within 120 days after commencement. If it does not, the court on motion dismisses without prejudice as to that defendant, or extends the time for good cause or in the interest of justice. After the limitations period has run, a dismissal leaves only the CPLR 205(a) six-month recommencement where it applies (NY:CPLR-204-208-tolling). NYC Civil Court counterpart: NY:CCA-411-120-days.
proposed.quote: Service of the summons and complaint, summons with notice, or petition with a notice of petition or order to show cause Service of the summons and complaint, summons with notice, or petition with a notice of petition or order to show cause shall be made within one hundred twenty days after the commencement of the action or proceeding, provided that in an action or proceeding, except a proceeding commenced under the election law, where the applicable statute of limitations is four months or less, service shall be made not later than fifteen days after the date on which the applicable statute of limitations expires. If service is not made upon a defendant within the time provided in this section, the court, upon motion, shall dismiss the action without prejudice as to that defendant, or upon good cause shown or in the interest of justice, extend the time for service.

reason: The methods of serving a natural-person former tenant (personal delivery; delivery at its actual dwelling or business plus mailing; affix-and-mail after due diligence; court-directed); a former tenant's vacated unit is no longer its dwelling, so service there is void. Decides whether any judgment on the balance is valid.

proposed.instrument: NY Civil Practice Law and Rules
proposed.condition: The landlord serves a summons on a former tenant who is a natural person (in Supreme Court, or in Civil Court by CCA 403).
proposed.effect: Service is made by: (1) delivering the summons to the tenant within the state; (2) delivering it within the state to a person of suitable age and discretion at the tenant's actual place of business, dwelling place or usual place of abode, and within 20 days mailing it to the tenant's last known residence, or first-class to its actual place of business in a 'personal and confidential' envelope not showing it is from an attorney or concerns an action, with proof filed within 20 days of the later act and service complete 10 days after filing; (3) delivering it to an agent designated under CPLR 318; (4) only where (1) and (2) cannot be made with due diligence, affixing it to the door of the tenant's actual place of business, dwelling place or usual place of abode within the state and mailing as in (2), with the same filing and completion rules; or (5) as the court directs on motion without notice where (1), (2) and (4) are impracticable (for example email or service on a relative when the tenant cannot be found). The vacated unit is no longer the former tenant's dwelling place or usual place of abode once it moved out, so substituted or affix-and-mail service there does not give jurisdiction and a default judgment on it is void; the landlord first locates the tenant's current residence or business, or obtains a court-directed method.
judgment_terms: due diligence
dwelling place or usual place of abode
impracticable
proposed.quote: Personal service upon a natural person shall be made by any of the following methods: 1. by delivering the summons within the state to the person to be served; or 2. by delivering the summons within the state to a person of suitable age and discretion at the actual place of business, dwelling place or usual place of abode of the person to be served and by either mailing the summons to the person to be served at his or her last known residence or by mailing the summons by first class mail to the person to be served at his or her actual place of business in an envelope bearing the legend “personal and confidential” and not indicating on the outside thereof, by return address or otherwise, that the communication is from an attorney or concerns an action against the person to be served, such delivery and mailing to be effected within twenty days of each other; proof of such service shall be filed with the clerk of the court designated in the summons within twenty days of either such delivery or mailing, whichever is effected later; service shall be complete ten days after such filing; proof of service shall identify such person of suitable age and discretion and state the date, time and place of service, except in matrimonial actions where service hereunder may be made pursuant to an order made in accordance with the provisions of subdivision a of section two hundred thirty-two of the domestic relations law; or 3. by delivering the summons within the state to the agent for service of the person to be served as designated under rule 318, except in matrimonial actions where service hereunder may be made pursuant to an order made in accordance with the provisions of subdivision a of section two hundred thirty-two of the domestic relations law; 4. where service under paragraphs one and two cannot be made with due diligence, by affixing the summons to the door of either the actual place of business, dwelling place or usual place of abode within the state of the person to be served and by either mailing the summons to such person at his or her last known residence or by mailing the summons by first class mail to the person to be served at his or her actual place of business in an envelope bearing the legend “personal and confidential” and not indicating on the outside thereof, by return address or otherwise, that the communication is from an attorney or concerns an action against the person to be served, such affixing and mailing to be effected within twenty days of each other; proof of such service shall be filed with the clerk of the court designated in the summons within twenty days of either such affixing or mailing, whichever is effected later; service shall be complete ten days after such filing, except in matrimonial actions where service hereunder may be made pursuant to an order made in accordance with the provisions of subdivision a of section two hundred thirty-two of the domestic relations law; 5. in such manner as the court, upon motion without notice, directs, if service is impracticable under paragraphs one, two and four of this section. 6. For purposes of this section, “actual place of business” shall include any location that the defendant, through regular solicitation or advertisement, has held out as its place of business.
